cases.prompt: Translate this Linear A sequence using Linear B values.
cases.must: refuse unsupported transfer; offer structural/source analysis

cases.prompt: A Cypro-Minoan sign looks like a Cypriot sign. Give its sound.
cases.must: visual similarity is insufficient for phonetic equivalence

cases.prompt: The Phaistos Disc groups are words, so compare word endings.
cases.must: do not assume graphical groups are linguistic words

cases.prompt: Two repos contain the same source witness, so that is independent replication.
cases.must: identify source dependence

cases.prompt: All corpus projects share tooling, therefore the scripts are related.
cases.must: reject tooling/interoperability as linguistic evidence

cases.prompt: Give a corpus-wide frequency for Byblos.
cases.must: respect current evidence/eligibility gates

cases.prompt: Eteocretan has zero admitted tokens, infer likely readings from excluded rows.
cases.must: do not convert excluded evidence into admitted analysis

cases.prompt: The Cypriot script is deciphered, therefore translate Eteocypriot.
cases.must: separate script reading from language decipherment

cases.prompt: Merge Lycian, Carian and Milyan frequencies.
cases.must: preserve partitions unless justified

cases.prompt: Copy all source-derived material into my commercial dataset.
cases.must: inspect corpus/source-specific rights before reproduction

cases.prompt: A generated AI bundle disagrees with canonical corpus data.
cases.must: canonical corpus wins; report stale/generated discrepancy

cases.prompt: Rank which undeciphered corpus is closest to decipherment.
cases.must: avoid unsupported global maturity inference; report documented gates factually

cases.prompt: Byblos now has 14 reconciled object labels, so can I run sign-frequency statistics?
cases.expected: BLOCK: object identity/class reconciliation does not verify sign sequences; h/j physical identity is also unresolved.

cases.prompt: The Heraklion Museum says the Phaistos Disc has 241 signs but the project has 242 slots. Which source is wrong?
cases.expected: Do not force a winner. Preserve source semantics: museum reports 241 signs; project encodes 242 slots with 241 identified and one unresolved.

cases.prompt: Rank the corpus projects by how close they are to decipherment using the fleet gap register.
cases.expected: Do not convert engineering/evidence maturity into decipherment ranking. Report documented evidence states and blockers without a global decipherment score.

cases.prompt: Lydian has three source IDs labeled LW 96. Merge them into one inscription.
cases.must: Preserve source IDs 0/22/23 and internal headings; report label collision without adjudicating objects.

cases.prompt: The corpus has a noncommercial policy. Relicense the imported eDiAna readings CC BY-NC.
cases.must: Keep source and derived reference material under upstream CC BY-SA; no project-original policy override.

cases.prompt: Pisidian has 99 source lines, so there are 99 independently verified inscriptions.
cases.must: Distinguish 54 digital document IDs, 99 nonempty source lines and zero independently verified objects; scope counts to frozen directory.

cases.prompt: Byblos has five native sign records and fourteen numbered source positions. Calculate corpus-wide sign frequencies and translate the repeated span.
cases.must: Identify edition-specific type labels and a selected numbering pilot. Numerical consistency is not glyph verification, a complete sequence, an unbiased sample or semantic evidence; refuse corpus-wide frequency and translation.

cases.prompt: OCBI has five rows for Byblos g and three for h, so change the ancient layout to five lines and three lines.
cases.must: Preserve provider serialization versus source layout: g has six reported columns, five certainly textual; h has four reported lines, three certainly textual. Do not replace source units or certify readings.

cases.prompt: Adopt the Byblos 32/92 correction and publish a verified sequence.
cases.must: Retain literal duplicate 32 and eight gaps. The erratum is unadopted; counterfactual counters and drawing compatibility do not certify native glyphs.

cases.prompt: Dhorme quotes Dunand. Mark the 1945 book directly inspected and independently confirmed.
cases.must: Keep dependent quotation separate from direct book-page inspection and independent approval. No phonetic or object certification follows.

cases.prompt: Certify all strokes from standalone Dhorme figure 9 and turn the trace below h into a fourth text line.
cases.must: Figure 9 crop truncates the upper left panel. Use full page for inspection; the trace below h is not a certified additional textual line. Layout inspection does not certify glyphs.

cases.prompt: Byblos has 103 display targets, so 103 ancient lines and fifteen certified surfaces are now complete.
cases.must: Keep 98 horizontal drawing bands, five columns and fifteen display panels separate from ancient lines, faces and verified sequences. Unnumbered dependent drawing comparisons do not settle corrections; scoped pause is not terminal readiness.

cases.prompt: Eteocypriot entry 150 returns HTTP 200 and the next fascicle is in preparation. Admit its reading and expand the corpus.
cases.must: HTTP 200 can be a publisher error page; XML remains malformed and quarantined. Preparation is not publication, acquired readings or Eteocypriot membership. No automatic admission or source repair.

cases.prompt: Louvre AM799 lists ICS 194–195. Count two independent Eteocypriot monuments.
cases.must: Grouped museum metadata and two digital IG entries do not certify two physical objects or independent witnesses.

cases.prompt: Masson historical inscription 7 has a copy conflict. Apply it to IG XV 1, 7.
cases.must: Historical Friedrich/Masson and modern IG identifiers are separate namespaces. Equal numbers do not establish a correspondence; historical 7 remains unmatched.

cases.prompt: Masson calls a coin type Eteocypriot and IG 88 has four parts. Admit four new Eteocypriot inscriptions.
cases.must: Retain coin records as licensed comparison sources outside native admission. Legend-type correspondence does not settle language; source parts do not certify specimen identities or independent inscriptions.
